[JEE Main 2022, 28 Jul (Shift 2)]

Given \(x=2\sqrt2\cos t\sqrt{\sin2t}\).

Differentiating with respect to \(t\),

\(\dfrac{dx}{dt}=2\sqrt2\left(-\sin t\sqrt{\sin2t}+\cos t\cdot\dfrac{\cos2t}{\sqrt{\sin2t}}\right)\)

\(\Rightarrow \dfrac{dx}{dt}=\dfrac{2\sqrt2}{\sqrt{\sin2t}}\left(-\sin t\sin2t+\cos t\cos2t\right)\)

Also, \(y=2\sqrt2\sin t\sqrt{\sin2t}\).

Differentiating with respect to \(t\),

\(\dfrac{dy}{dt}=2\sqrt2\left(\cos t\sqrt{\sin2t}+\sin t\cdot\dfrac{\cos2t}{\sqrt{\sin2t}}\right)\)

\(\Rightarrow \dfrac{dy}{dt}=\dfrac{2\sqrt2}{\sqrt{\sin2t}}\left(\cos t\sin2t+\sin t\cos2t\right)\)

\(\Rightarrow \dfrac{dy}{dt}=\dfrac{2\sqrt2\sin3t}{\sqrt{\sin2t}}\)

\(\Rightarrow \dfrac{dy}{dx}=\tan3t\)

questions.question:
The function \(f(x)=x e^{x(1-x)}, x \in \mathbb{R}\) is

 

[JEE Main 2022, 28 Jul (Shift 2)]
questions.explanation:
The function is \(f(x)=xe^{x(1-x)}\)

Using the product rule,

\(f'(x)=1\cdot e^{x(1-x)}+x\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(e^{x(1-x)}\right)\)

By the chain rule,

\(\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(e^{x(1-x)}\right)=e^{x(1-x)}\dfrac{d}{dx}(x-x^2)\)

Therefore, \(\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(e^{x(1-x)}\right)=e^{x(1-x)}(1-2x)\)

Hence, \(f'(x)=e^{x(1-x)}+xe^{x(1-x)}(1-2x)\)

Taking \(e^{x(1-x)}\) common,

\(f'(x)=e^{x(1-x)}[1+x-2x^2]\)

We have \(1+x-2x^2=-(2x^2-x-1)\)

Also, \(2x^2-x-1=(2x+1)(x-1)\)

Therefore, \(1+x-2x^2=(1-x)(2x+1)\)

Hence, \(f'(x)=e^{x(1-x)}(1-x)(2x+1)\)

Since \(e^{x(1-x)}>0\) for every real \(x\)

the sign of \(f'(x)\) depends on \((1-x)(2x+1)\)

The critical values are \(x=1\) and \(x=-\dfrac12\)

For \(x<-\dfrac12\), \(1-x>0\) and \(2x+1<0\),

so \(f'(x)<0\)

For \(-\dfrac12<x<1\), \(1-x>0\) and \(2x+1>0\),

so \(f'(x)>0\)

For \(x>1\), \(1-x<0\) and \(2x+1>0\),

so \(f'(x)<0\)

Therefore, the function is increasing on \(\left(-\dfrac12,1\right)\)

A plane \( P \) is parallel to two lines whose direction ratios are \( -2,1,-3 \) and \( -1,2,-2 \) and it contains the point \( (2,2,-2) \). Let \( P \) intersect the coordinate axis at the points \( A, B \) and \( C \) making the intercepts \( \alpha, \beta \) and \( \gamma \). If \( V \) is the volume of the tetrahedron \( \mathrm{O} A B C \), where \( \mathrm{O} \) is the origin and \( p=\alpha+\beta+\gamma \) then the ordered pair \( (V, p) \) is equal to

 

[JEE Main 2022, 28 Jul (Shift 2)]
questions.explanation:
The given direction vectors parallel to the plane are \(\vec d_1=(-2,1,-3)\) and \(\vec d_2=(-1,2,-2)\).

A normal vector of the plane is

\(\vec n=\vec d_1\times\vec d_2=(4,-1,-3)\)

The plane passes through \((2,2,-2)\).

\(4(x-2)-(y-2)-3(z+2)=0\)

\(\Rightarrow 4x-y-3z-12=0\)

The \(x\)-intercept is obtained by putting \(y=0\) and \(z=0\).

\(4x-12=0\)

\(\Rightarrow \alpha=3\)

The \(y\)-intercept is obtained by putting \(x=0\) and \(z=0\).

\(-y-12=0\)

\(\Rightarrow \beta=-12\)

The \(z\)-intercept is obtained by putting \(x=0\) and \(y=0\).

\(-3z-12=0\)

\(\Rightarrow \gamma=-4\)

The volume of tetrahedron \(OABC\) is

\(V=\dfrac{1}{6}|\alpha\beta\gamma|\)

\(\Rightarrow V=\dfrac{1}{6}|3(-12)(-4)|=24\)

\(p=\alpha+\beta+\gamma=3-12-4=-13\)

\(\Rightarrow (V,p)=(24,-13)\)

The correct option is \(\mathrm{B}\).

[JEE Main 2022, 28 Jul (Shift 2)]
questions.explanation:
For the first line, take

\(A=(1,2,3),\quad \vec d_1=(\lambda,1,2)\)

For the second line, take

\(B=(-26,-18,-28),\quad \vec d_2=(-2,3,\lambda)\)

The lines are coplanar when

\(\overrightarrow{AB}\cdot(\vec d_1\times\vec d_2)=0\)

\(\overrightarrow{AB}=(-27,-20,-31)\)

\(\vec d_1\times\vec d_2=(\lambda-6,-\lambda^2-4,3\lambda+2)\)

\(\Rightarrow -27(\lambda-6)-20(-\lambda^2-4)-31(3\lambda+2)=0\)

\(\Rightarrow 20\lambda^2-120\lambda+180=0\)

\(\Rightarrow 20(\lambda-3)^2=0\)

\(\Rightarrow \lambda=3\)

A normal of the plane containing the lines is

\((3,1,2)\times(-2,3,3)=(-3,-13,11)\)

Using \(A=(1,2,3)\), the plane is

\(-3(x-1)-13(y-2)+11(z-3)=0\)

\(\Rightarrow -3x-13y+11z-4=0\)

For \((0,-2,-2)\), the left side is \(0\).

For \((-5,0,-1)\), the left side is \(0\).

For \((3,-1,0)\), the left side is \(0\).

For \((0,4,5)\), the left side is \(-1\), so this point does not lie on the plane.

The correct option is \(\mathrm{D}\).

Let \(A\) and \(B\) be two events such that \(P(B \mid A)=\frac{2}{5}, P(A \mid B)=\frac{1}{7}\) and \(P(A \cap B)=\frac{1}{9}\).

Consider \((S 1):  P\left(A^{\prime} \cup B\right)=\frac{5}{6}\)

\((S 2):  P\left(A^{\prime} \cap B^{\prime}\right)=\frac{1}{18}\)

 

[JEE Main 2022, 28 Jul (Shift 2)]
questions.explanation:
\(
\begin{aligned}
& P(A |B)=\frac{1}{7} \Rightarrow \frac{P(A \cap B)}{P(B)}=\frac{1}{7} \\
& \Rightarrow P(B)=\frac{7}{9} \\
& P(B |A)=\frac{2}{5} \Rightarrow \frac{P(A \cap B)}{P(A)}=\frac{2}{5} \\
& \Rightarrow P(A)=\frac{5}{18}
\end{aligned}
\)

Now,
\(
\begin{aligned}
& P\left(A^{\prime} \cup B\right)=1-P(A \cup B)+P(B) \\
& =1-P(A)+P(A \cap B)=\frac{5}{6} \\
& P\left(A^{\prime} \cap B^{\prime}\right)=1-P(A \cup B) \\
& =1-P(A)-P(B)+P(A \cap B)=\frac{1}{18}
\end{aligned}
\)

Both \(\left(S_1\right)\) and \(\left(S_2\right)\) are true.

questions.question:
Let \(z=a+i b, b \neq 0\) be complex numbers satisfying \(z^2=\bar{z} \cdot 2^{1-|z|}\). Then the least value of \(n \in N\), such that \(z^n\) \(=(z+1)^n\), is equal to.

 

[JEE Main 2022, 28 Jul (Shift 2)]
questions.explanation:
\(|z^2|=|\bar z|\cdot 2^{1-|z|}\)

\(\Rightarrow |z|^2=|z|\cdot 2^{1-|z|}\)

Since \(z\neq0\), divide by \(|z|\).

\(\Rightarrow |z|=2^{1-|z|}\)

This gives \(|z|=1\).

Also,

\(z^2=\bar z\)

Since \(|z|=1\), we have \(\bar z=\dfrac{1}{z}\).

So,

\(z^2=\dfrac{1}{z}\)

\(\Rightarrow z^3=1\)

\(\Rightarrow z=1,\omega,\omega^2\)

For \(z=1\), \(z^n=(1+z)^n\) gives \(1^n=2^n\), which is not possible for any natural number \(n\).

So, \(z=\omega\) or \(z=\omega^2\).

For \(z=\omega\),

\(1+\omega=-\omega^2\)

So,

\(\omega^n=(1+\omega)^n\)

\(\Rightarrow \omega^n=(-\omega^2)^n\)

\(\Rightarrow \omega^n=(-1)^n\omega^{2n}\)

\(\Rightarrow 1=(-1)^n\omega^n\)

The least natural value satisfying this is \(n=6\).

For \(z=\omega^2\),

\(1+\omega^2=-\omega\)

So,

\((\omega^2)^n=(1+\omega^2)^n\)

\(\Rightarrow \omega^{2n}=(-\omega)^n\)

\(\Rightarrow \omega^{2n}=(-1)^n\omega^n\)

\(\Rightarrow \omega^n=(-1)^n\)

The least natural value satisfying this is also \(n=6\).

Hence, the least natural value of \(n\) is \(6\).

questions.question:
A bag contains 4 white and 6 black balls. Three balls are drawn at random from the bag. Let \(X\) be the number of white balls, among the drawn balls. If \(\sigma^2\) is the variance of \(X\), then \(100 \sigma^2\) is equal to.........

 

[JEE Main 2022, 28 Jul (Shift 2)]
questions.explanation:
Let \(X\) be the number of white balls among the three selected balls.

There are \(10\) balls, of which \(4\) are white.

\(\displaystyle E(X)=3\cdot\dfrac{4}{10}=\dfrac{6}{5}\)

For two ordered positions among the three draws,

\(\displaystyle E\bigl(X(X-1)\bigr)=3\cdot2\cdot\dfrac{4}{10}\cdot\dfrac{3}{9}=\dfrac{4}{5}\)

\(\displaystyle E(X^2)=E\bigl(X(X-1)\bigr)+E(X)=\dfrac{4}{5}+\dfrac{6}{5}=2\)

\(\displaystyle \sigma^2=\operatorname{Var}(X)=2-\left(\dfrac{6}{5}\right)^2=\dfrac{14}{25}\)

\(\displaystyle 100\sigma^2=100\cdot\dfrac{14}{25}=56\)

The required value is \(56\).
